prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the 3D layout of a cluttered garage across the 5 frames as the camera wearer looks up from the floor and turns around a wooden cabinet: in frames 1–2, a person's torso at the far right edge (<0.5 m) and the upright wooden shelving unit next to them (0.5–1.5 m) are brightest and within arm's reach, while two wooden drawers and a floor lamp sit 1.5–2.5 m away on the floor to the left. Across frames 3–5, the wooden cabinet remains in the immediate foreground (0.5–1.5 m, within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the second person) and occludes the lower body of the blonde person in the teal shirt, who stands 1–1.5 m away to the left of the cabinet in frames 3–4 (facing right toward the cabinet and looking down, not at the camera wearer) before shifting to 1.5 m behind the cabinet in frame 5. Behind them at 3–5 m are a green lawn tractor on the right (frames 3–4), a back wall with a door and high shelves above, and an open garage doorway on the left in frame 5. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates foreground cabinet surfaces and the person's head/torso from the busy garage background and shows continuous metric-like depth gradients along the top of the cabinet and floor. However, the map is unreliable on thin structures like the lamp pole and multi-head shades (which disappear or merge into the dark background in frames 3–5) and flattens detailed background clutter beyond 3 m into nearly uniform dark values.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only a few discrete foreground and mid-ground regions against the garage scene: in frame 1, it detects the person in the teal shirt at the right edge (<0.5 m, within arm's reach and mostly out of the frame) as 'person', while in frames 4 and 5 it tracks that same person standing 1–1.5 m away to the left of and then behind the wooden cabinet (within arm's reach of the cabinet, facing toward the cabinet rather than the camera wearer, with their lower body occluded by it). In frame 3, the map segments the combined silhouette of the person (1 m away on the left) and the foreground wooden cabinet (0.5–1.5 m in front) together as a single mask, and outlines the green lawn tractor 3–4 m behind the cabinet on the right. While the sharp mask contours in frames 1, 4, and 5 help isolate the person's visible upper-body boundary from the visually cluttered garage shelving and tools behind them, the segmentation map is highly unreliable across the strip. It completely misses the wooden shelving and drawers in frame 2, merges the person and wooden cabinet into a false 'bed' class in frame 3, misclassifies the background lawn tractor as a 'motorcycle' in frame 3, and hallucinates 'person' on the upper-left purple lamp shade in frame 1 (~2 m away) and 'cup' on a tiny floor fragment in frame 4.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand pose map is completely black across all 5 frames, failing to detect any yellow body skeletons or magenta hand skeletons despite a second person being present in frames 1, 3, 4, and 5. In the RGB strip, this person is visible within 0.5 m at the right edge of frame 1 (showing only their back/shoulder and left arm within arm's reach) and at 1–1.5 m in frames 3–5 standing to the left of and then behind the foreground wooden cabinet (0.5–1.5 m away, within arm's reach of both people), facing and looking downward toward the cabinet rather than toward the camera wearer. Because the person's lower body and hands are largely occluded by the wooden cabinet and truncated by the bottom and side frame boundaries, and their face and torso are motion-blurred in frames 4–5 as the camera turns, the pose estimator produces no skeletal keypoints to indicate facing direction, reach, or joint movement. Consequently, the pose map adds no spatial information beyond RGB and is entirely unreliable on these heavily occluded, truncated, and blurred egocentric views.
